summary.en: Israel has intensified airstrikes and artillery shelling on southern Lebanon, targeting Hezbollah rocket sites, launchers in the Beqaa Valley, and other facilities, while drones have flown over Beirut. Hezbollah is reportedly using fishing boats to spy on the Israeli navy and Israel is employing Christian villages in south Lebanon in a divide-and-conquer effort. Hezbollah’s leader has again demanded the release of five detained operatives and rejected any post-UNIFIL force outside U.N. authority, as both sides prepare for an eighth round of peace talks before year-end. The conflict has caused 4,335 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Israel har økt luftangrep og artilleriskudd i Sør-Lebanon, med mål på Hizbollahs rakettsteder, avfyringsramper i Bekaa-dalen og andre anlegg, mens droner har fløyet over Beirut. Ifølge rapporter bruker Hizbollah fiskebåter til å spionere på den israelske marinen, og Israel bruker kristne landsbyer i Sør-Lebanon i en del-og-hersk-strategi. Hizbollahs leder har igjen krevd løslatelse av fem fengslede operatører og avvist enhver styrke etter UNIFIL utenfor FN myndighet, mens begge sider forbereder den åttende runden med fredssamtaler før årsskiftet. Ifølge UCDP har konflikten forårsaket 4 335 dødsfall i kamp i 2024.

background.title: Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)
background.extract: An ongoing conflict between the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah and Israel began on 8 October 2023, when Hezbollah launched rockets and artillery at Israeli positions following Hamas's October 7 attacks on Israel. The conflict escalated into a prolonged exchange of bombardments, leading to extensive displacement in Israel and Lebanon. The conflict is part of the broader Middle Eastern crisis that began with Hamas's attack, with the short Israeli invasion of Lebanon in 2024 marking the largest escalation of the Hezbollah–Israel conflict since the 2006 Lebanon War. In Arabic, the conflict (2023–2024) is referred to as the "Support War" or the "Gaza Support War."
